parole.significato: akim, a leader of a local administration in Kazakhstan or Kyrgyzstan
parole.testo: Borrowed from Kazakh әкім (äkim) or Kyrgyz аким (akim).

parole.significato: A (generally Turkic-speaking or Asian and typically older or married) woman
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Turkic language, such as Kazakh апай (apay), with addition of -ка (-ka).

parole.significato: barchan, sand dune (formed by the wind into a crescent shape)
dombra (long-necked lute of Turkic or Central Asian origin)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Kazakh домбыра (dombıra), from Persian دنب بره (donb-e barre, literally “lamb's tail”). Related to Ottoman Turkish طنبوره (tanbura/tambura), Turkish tambura, Romanian tambură, Arabic طُنْبُور (ṭunbūr), etc. Doublet of до́мра (dómra) and танбу́р (tanbúr).

parole.significato: title of a head of state in Kazakhstan
zhuz, horde, a Kazakh clan or tribal division

parole.testo: From Kazakh қазақ (qazaq), from Old Turkic 𐰴𐰔𐰍𐰴 (qazǧaq, “profiteer”), from 𐰴𐰔𐰍𐰣𐰢𐰴 (qazǧanmaq, “to acquire”), from 𐰴𐰔𐰢𐰴 (qazmaq, “to dig out”), from Proto-Turkic *kaŕ-. Doublet of каза́к (kazák, “Cossack”). Russian [x] possibly reflects the Kazakh allaphony of the phoneme /q/ to [χ], i.e. қазақ /qaz

parole.significato: a large bag in which cotton is collected
parole.testo: Borrowed from Kazakh қанар (qanar) (Uzbek qanor), from Persian کنار (kanâr, “side, edge, border”) apparently because the sack was to the side of man, or the sacks were at the border of the field, during reaping.
1920s, from Kazakh лобия (lobıya), from Persian لوبیا (lôbiyâ).

parole.significato: a rural Kazakh person, perceived to be uneducated.
parole.testo: From Kazakh Мәмбет (Mämbet), a popular name among Kazakh men, which is also used in Kazakh slang to refer to a country bumpkin or yokel; ultimately Arabic مُحَمَّد (muḥammad). Sense 5 was most likely brought to Yakutia from soldiers returning from the Soviet Army.
1920s, from Kazakh мәш (mäš), from Persian ماش (mâš)
Borrowed from Kazakh тақыр (taqır) and other Turkic languages.

parole.significato: to pot, put a child on the potty
parole.testo: Borrowed from Kazakh тосу (tosuw, “to pot a child”).
Attested at least since 1780s, akin to later attested Russian тушкан (tuškan), from Kazakh тышқан (tıšqan, “mouse”), from Proto-Turkic *sïčgan.

Borrowed from Kazakh тышқан (tıšqan, “mouse”), influenced by Russian у́хо (úxo, “ear”). By surface analysis, from у́шко́ (úškó, diminutive of у́хо (úxo, “ear”)) + -ан (-an). Doublet of тушка́нчик (tuškánčik).
